name: co-authored-commit-spanning-two-orgs
description: SCOPE §11.4 + TODO §0.2 regression. A commit authored by user U1 with co-author U2 lands once in the store but is visible in two orgs (a fork merged across an org boundary — the same activity_event row carries the same event_id while the EventActorRow projection joins it once per (org, role) pairing). The all_orgs_combined lens must dedup on (user_id, event_id) so U1 is credited once and U2 once, not twice each. The single_org lens on either org must credit each contributor once for that org. A second, unrelated org-B commit by U2 is included so totals are distinguishable from a naive 'collapse everything' bug.
github_recorded_payload_ref: Synthesized from the GitHub REST response shape documented at https://docs.github.com/en/rest/commits/commits — verbatim raw payload is not checked in to keep this regression hermetic.

checks.name: all_orgs_combined: co-authored commit credits each contributor once across both orgs
single_org A: each contributor credited once for the shared commit
single_org B: A1+A2 from shared commit, plus the extra org-B-only commit by U2
